text:
tara (release lead): deploy-bot popped an alert on canary for inference-service v3.1.0 — p95 jumped and a couple of timeouts. change window in 18m.

deploy-bot: ALERT: canary rollout: inference-service v3.1.0 exceeded p95 latency threshold (threshold=250ms, observed=390ms). Auto-rollback eligibility: true. Suggested action: review.
joe (sre): seeing connection timeouts from worker-7, GPU mem pressure coincident with long decode loops. traces show increased KV writes.
hema (eng): recent change in 3.1.0: aggressive kvprefetch + async eviction. could be thrashing cache when context size grows. suspect workload pattern on canary slice.
rachel (pm): any dedicated customers pinned to 3.1.0 already? what's blast radius?
ops-oncall: no dedicated pools pinned yet. Hosted canary is ~5% traffic across us-west-2. eu region unaffected today.
joe (sre): telemetry's sparse if autopilot rolls back — we lose canary traces that show transition. i prefer manual pin so we can keep traces for root cause.
hema (eng): +1 to manual pin. i can craft a minimal revert for kvprefetch tomorrow AM if we pin now.
tara (release lead): deploy-bot says auto-rollback eligible. pros of auto: fast recovery. cons: loses post-failure traces; customers see less churn. we need to pick.
deploy-bot: NOTE: /deploy rollback --service=inference-service --to=3.0.8 --scope=canary --reason="p95 spike" OR /deploy pin-version --service=inference-service --version=3.0.8 --scope=canary
joe (sre): manual pin workflow is quick. i'll run pin and then run a 10m smoke plus a synthetic with long context.
rachel (pm): i'll prepare a single-sentence customer note in #customer-briefing if we pin. keep it calm: "We detected and contained a latency regression. Canary rolled back while we investigate. No action required."
tara (release lead): decision: manual pin to 3.0.8 for canary. hema, prioritize revert PR; joe, run pin and smoke; rachel, draft comms; ops, postpone wider rollout.
joe (sre): running:
```
/bin/deployctl pin-version --service inference-service --version 3.0.8 --scope canary --note "p95 regression: kvprefetch eviction"
# pin should take ~90s
```
joe (sre): pin complete. canary shifted back to 3.0.8. starting synthetic long-context run.
joe (sre): synthetic run done, no timeouts. p95 trending down toward baseline. :white_check_mark:
hema (eng): PR opened: revert-kvprefetch-async (https://git.redwood/repo/pull/912). added an integration test for large context sequence.
ops-oncall: change window updated: hold 3.1.0 rollout until revert validated and staging smoke passes. scheduled follow-up deploy tomorrow 08:00 UTC.
tara (release lead): update release notes with short rollback entry and rationale (manual pin to preserve telemetry). also add a runbook note about criteria for choosing manual pin vs autopilot.
rachel (pm): drafted note and queued to post after 20m stable: "We observed a performance regression in a small canary during today's rollout of v3.1.0 and rolled back the canary to v3.0.8 while the engineering team investigates. No customer action required."
joe (sre): 20m stable, metrics flat, no regressions observed. will unpin after we validate the revert in staging and schedule re-rollout.
tara (release lead): thanks team. closing thread — manual pin executed, PR in flight, comms queued, follow-up deploy scheduled."
